name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,254

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Local outside has left hosts well-informed about burrowing mammals

indicators.note: the letters on the outside of the word have gone away, so both ends are stripped off
a host takes guests in, so the trimmed word holds the next phrase inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, before its outer letters are dropped
to be hot on a subject is to know it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A local expert steps outside and leaves visitors well briefed on animals that live underground.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCAL loses its two outer Ls to leave OCA, which then wraps HOT ON to give OCHOTONA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochotona is the zoological genus of the pikas, small rabbit-like creatures that dig and live in burrows.

clue.text: Hold covers with both hands — it was careless to grasp that

indicators.note: grasping something means holding it tight inside, so the exclamation wraps round the pair of hand letters

blocks.note: what you exclaim after a careless slip
right and left, one letter for each hand

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy grabs the lids with both hands and blurts out an apology.
explanation.walkthrough: OOPS takes in R and L after its first letter, giving ORLOPS.
explanation.definitionFit: An orlop is the lowest deck of a ship, laid over the cargo space below as its ceiling.

clue.text: Pickle welcome at party

blocks.note: an informal greeting
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone greeting guests at a party with a jar of pickles.
explanation.definitionFit: A howdy-do is an informal word for an awkward mess or predicament, just as a pickle is.

clue.text: The first course? Fish, to serve once

blocks.note: a trail is a path or course to follow
A is the first letter, and also stands for first class
a predatory freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A menu question: is the opening course of the dinner a fish dish?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a dinner menu, but course means a route here, and serve means doing military service, not bringing plates to a table.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail a pike was an old idiom for soldiering, since infantry once carried the long pole weapon.

clue.text: Old women at summit maybe to get in a buggy: the other one runs up

indicators.note: something buggy is faulty and garbled, so the preceding words come out jumbled
in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

blocks.note: the letters to be jumbled
the other is a coy euphemism for sexual intercourse
the Roman numeral for one
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Two women try to clamber into a buggy while a third dashes up to join them.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled letters of TO GET IN A make NEGOTIAT, then SEX, I and R read upwards add RIXES.
explanation.definitionFit: A negotiatrix is an old feminine form of negotiator, the sort of envoy who bargains at a summit meeting.

clue.text: Minor fiction genre, mostly recalled term at Nanterre for Oxonian?

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped
called back, so the letters run back the way they came

blocks.note: a fib is a small, trivial lie
a genre is a kind or sort

explanation.surface: A literature student notes a slight genre of fiction and a term remembered from a stay in France.
explanation.walkthrough: FIB plus SOR (SORT minus T) is FIBSOR, which read backwards gives ROSBIF. Nanterre is a Paris suburb; an Oxonian is a person from Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosbif, literally roast beef, is French slang for an English person, such as someone from Oxford.

clue.text: Old fellow in SA oddly missing for US play

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions go missing, so only the even-numbered ones are kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these words

explanation.surface: An elderly South African man is oddly absent from an American stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: Oupa is the Afrikaans word for grandfather, used in South Africa for any elderly man.

clue.text: Pup taken from counter, missing a long time

indicators.note: something missing has been lost, so the letter named next is removed from the word before it

blocks.note: a bar is the counter where drinks are served
the letter that goes missing
to long for something is to ache for it
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A puppy snatched from a shop counter has been lost for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: A long time looks like one phrase meaning ages, but it splits into three: a letter to remove, a verb for yearning, and an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A brachet is an old word for a small scenting hound, and the term is also used for a young hound.

clue.text: Unknown boxer punching what must be something naturally containing iron

indicators.note: a punch lands inside its target, so the boxer pair goes into the middle of the next word

blocks.note: fate is whatever is bound to happen
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns
Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight champion

explanation.surface: A boxer nobody has heard of throws punches at something inevitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fayalite is a mineral, the iron-rich silicate of the olivine group, which occurs naturally in rocks.

clue.text: Grade for one barely warmed up

blocks.note: first meaning: ... Grade, the British television mogul, is one person with this first name
second meaning: an old word for lukewarm

explanation.walkthrough: Grade looks like a school mark, but it is the surname of Lew Grade, a famous British entertainment impresario.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename belongs to the impresario Grade, and the dialect adjective means tepid, only slightly heated.

clue.text: A set right out of eg Oliver Twist in New York making appearance in such as It’s A Wonderful Life?

definitions.text: appearance in such as It’s A Wonderful Life?

indicators.note: out of means taken away from, so the right letter leaves the word that follows
these pieces are placed inside the abbreviation for the city

blocks.note: taken as written
the usual abbreviation for New York
jelly gels when it sets
the standard abbreviation for right
Dickens's hero has no parents

explanation.surface: A film buff sets a Dickens orphan in New York, as in a classic Christmas movie.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 1946 film It's A Wonderful Life an angel, Clarence, comes down to save the hero, which is why the question mark is there.
explanation.definitionFit: An angelophany is the visible manifestation of an angel to humans, like Clarence turning up in the Capra film.

clue.text: Princeton’s lax when reforming rules handed down?

indicators.note: reforming means forming again in a new shape, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Princeton University is slack about overhauling its traditional regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means unwritten law: common law passed on by custom and precedent rather than statute.

clue.text: Leaves arrangement of pub chain in the main, after retiring: ten acquired by Yankees

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so the island chain is written backwards
what is acquired is held, so the Yankees enclose the other pieces

blocks.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
Y is Yankee in the NATO alphabet, and there are two
an atoll is a ring of coral islands, and the main is the open sea
the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A pub chain's seaside branches are reorganised after retirements, and ten are bought by American investors.
explanation.walkthrough: Pub chain wants to be one phrase, but the pub and the chain are separate pieces, and the main is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Phyllotaxy is the botanical term for the pattern in which foliage is set out along a plant stem.

clue.text: Indian’s one to beat: keep cycling?

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the last letter rotates round to the front

blocks.note: to keep something is to hold it

explanation.surface: An Indian cyclist is the rider everyone else must beat to stay in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The D at the end of HOLD moves round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhol is a large double-headed drum from India, struck with sticks, so it is something an Indian musician beats.

clue.text: Tool for cutting vital with hot, not cold, salad getting left out

indicators.note: with one thing, not another, means the first letter takes the place of the second
getting something out means removing it, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: key means crucial or vital
a cabbage salad
the tap abbreviation for hot
the tap abbreviation for cold
the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A recipe note: hot salad, not a cold one, with something vital left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot and cold are the H and C on taps; the salad changes one letter and drops another before following the vital word.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyhole saw is a narrow-bladed handsaw for cutting curves and small openings in wood or board.

clue.text: Empty casino with gym needed by a climber in the tropics

indicators.note: an empty word has had its middle cleared out, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of casino
W is a common abbreviation for with
physical education, the school gym lesson
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deserted casino with a gym, needed by a mountaineer holidaying near the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: Climber suggests a mountaineer, but here it is a plant that climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowpea, or black-eyed pea, is a twining legume grown widely as a crop in hot tropical regions.

clue.text: Duck to release, with one taking turn to catch bird

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket
to vent is to let out or release
in playground chasing games, the player whose turn it is to chase is it

explanation.surface: A duck is let go, while someone takes a turn trying to catch a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is O in cricket, where a batter out without scoring is out for a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Oven-tit is an old country name for the willow warbler, a small songbird, from its domed oven-like nest.

clue.text: Notices with delight that bases have been removed from French arch

indicators.note: in a down entry the base of each word is its bottom letter, and those are taken away

blocks.note: espies means catches sight of
glee is great delight

explanation.surface: Someone notices with pleasure that the foundations of a French arch have been taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: ESPIES and GLEE each lose their final letter. Arch looks like a curved structure here, but it is the adjective meaning mischievous.
explanation.definitionFit: Espiègle is a French borrowing meaning roguish or playfully mischievous, the same sense as arch as an adjective.

clue.text: One dropping bottles close to work old drinks dispenser

indicators.note: to bottle something is to shut it inside, so the outer word encloses a letter
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: a sinker is a weight that drops a fishing line down
final letter of work

explanation.surface: A clumsy barman who keeps dropping bottles near the end of his shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinker was an archaic word for a tapster or cupbearer, one who poured out liquor for others.

clue.text: Unhealthy condition of writing material, one might suppose, for Zulu leaders

blocks.note: what a pen writes with
-osis is the medical suffix for a diseased state

explanation.surface: A doctor diagnoses a disease caught from pens and paper.
explanation.walkthrough: One might suppose admits the joke: the word looks like a medical name for an ink disorder, but it is something quite different.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkosi is the Zulu title for a chief or king, and this is its plural form in English.

clue.text: Scene on which to direct one acting up in East London?

definitions.text: one acting up in East London?

blocks.note: SC is the script abbreviation for scene
the helm is the wheel or tiller used to steer a ship

explanation.surface: A stage scene in which a director coaches an actor playing a Cockney.
explanation.walkthrough: East London looks like the Cockney end of the British capital, but it is a city in South Africa's Eastern Cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Schelm is a South African word for a rogue or rascal, someone who behaves badly, from Dutch.

clue.text: Plant to hang without trying to put down new ones

indicators.note: putting something down means setting it aside, so the letter for new is taken out and placed lower

blocks.note: a lynching is a hanging without a trial
the standard abbreviation for new
I is the Roman one, and two of them are I's

explanation.surface: A gardener suspends a pot without trying to bed in fresh plants.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter for new is moved lower down the word, after the CH. Trying means holding a trial here, not making an effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Lychnis is a genus of flowering plants in the pink family, including campions and ragged robin.

clue.text: Article on a king is sour stuff

blocks.note: the indefinite article
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
taken as written
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a king turns out to be bitter reading.
explanation.walkthrough: On is LEG because a cricket field's leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Alegar is vinegar made from soured ale, a sharp acidic liquid used like malt vinegar.

clue.text: Reserved a thousand blocks — gross appearing

indicators.note: a blockage sits stuck inside a passage, so the thousand letter is lodged within the other word

blocks.note: an icy manner is cold and reserved
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: A thousand seats are held back, blocking the view and looking unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Icky is informal for disgusting or distasteful, the slangy sense of gross meaning revolting.

clue.text: Husband being with wife’s family’s universal sort of logic: “I like a healthy diet?”

blocks.note: U is the film-certificate letter for universal
exclusive or, an operation in Boolean logic
taken as written
lo-cal, low in calories

explanation.surface: A husband living with his in-laws insists his diet choices follow universal logic.
explanation.walkthrough: XOR is the logic gate that is true when exactly one input is true; lo-cal is a punning way of reading local.
explanation.definitionFit: Uxorilocal is the anthropologists' term for marriage customs where the couple settle with the bride's relatives.

clue.text: Turned up three or four contracts for woodcutter

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
the phrase contracts the answer in the sense of containing it within its run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and into the last

explanation.surface: A few business contracts arrived for a lumberjack.
explanation.walkthrough: The run EORF sits across thrEE OR Four, and read upwards gives FROE. Woodcutter looks like a person but is a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A froe is a cleaving tool with a blade set at right angles to its handle, used to split timber into shingles.

clue.text: Expert diners grasp host so roughly

indicators.note: done roughly means handled crudely, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Gourmet guests seize their host rather roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastrosophs are connoisseurs of fine eating, people skilled in the art of good food.

clue.text: Dun horse?

blocks.note: first meaning: to dun is to press someone persistently, as for a debt
second meaning: an old or worn-out horse

explanation.walkthrough: Dun looks like the greyish-brown colour of a horse, but here it is the verb for pestering a debtor.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for pestering someone repeatedly and a noun for an elderly, tired steed.

clue.text: Stand guarding singer originally in One Direction, in Dollar?

indicators.note: guarding means standing round something, so the outer word surrounds the single letter
originally points to how the word begins, so only its first letter is used

blocks.note: an easel is a stand for a painting
first letter of singer

explanation.surface: Security stand guard over a singer from the boy band One Direction, paid in dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: One Direction looks like the boy band, but it is a compass bearing. Dollar is a small town in central Scotland, so the word is Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Eassel is a Scots adverb meaning eastward, towards one compass point, as someone in a Scottish town might say.

clue.text: Measure for travellers that was considerably smarter

blocks.note: way is informal for very much, as in way better
wiser means more intelligent

explanation.surface: A gadget for tourists that proved a lot cleverer than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A waywiser is an old instrument with a wheel that records the distance covered along a road.
